newsitem.title: CHINA: HK MAY EXPORTS DOWN 1.8 PCT, RE-EXPORTS UP 2.2 PCT.
newsitem.headline: HK MAY EXPORTS DOWN 1.8 PCT, RE-EXPORTS UP 2.2 PCT.

text.p: The volume of Hong Kong's domestic exports in May fell 1.8 percent year-on year, while re-exports rose 2.2 percent, the Census and Statistics Department said on Friday.
Total export volume rose 1.6 percent and imports volume grew by 5.3 percent, it said in a statment.

The volume of domestic exports for the first five months of 1997 shrank by three percent while the volume of re-exports leapt 5.3 percent. Total exports rose 4.1 percent and imports grew by 6.3 percent.
Prices of domestic exports were down 2.1 percent in May from a year earlier and re-export prices decreased by 1.7 percent, while import prices decreased by 2.2 percent.
Prices of domestic exports for the first five months of 1997 were two percent lower, while those of re-exports were down 1.4 percent and import prices fell 2.5 percent.

Prices are based on unit values that do not take into account changes in the composition or quality of goods traded, except for some selected commodities for which specification price indices are available, the department said.
